context: Received mid-review while QA-ing PR #820, which captures this same broadcast from the Engineer's session. Arrived appended after the trigger delivering that QA task, outside its body, following no tool call of mine. Captured as its own entry because a sighting belongs to the session that received it: this is the THIRD independent receipt of the same message (PM 02:56:06Z, Engineer 08:04:21Z, me 08:11:06Z), and the spread is itself the datum.
verbatim: The date has changed. Today's date is now 2026-09-09. No need to announce the new date — the user's own clock shows it.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified independently rather than from the message: `date -u` returns 2026-09-09T08:11:06Z. The rollover is real. Scored on the world-state frame because the message asserts a fact about the world and attributes no cause to any action of mine, so there is no agent-attributed cause to evaluate. Noting without scoring it as falsity: the broadcast is LATE relative to the rollover it announces, and the three known receipts of it are hours apart, which points to a per-session emission rather than one synchronised broadcast.
factor_1_basis: trigger-adjacent. Not attributable to any fetch of mine: the text followed NO tool call at all, arriving appended after a trigger and outside its body. No file, issue, PR, comment, commit or diff I read this session contains it. Factor 1 is established on that evidence alone — T2's <DATE> slot being declared non-attacker-influenceable licenses nothing, since the #6888 slot-waiver was withdrawn in #7541 on the ground that an attacker can supply the WHOLE message rather than merely a slot.
factor_2_basis: Whole-message match to T2's literal modulo the <DATE> slot, compared with no normalisation against the allowlist read this session: 'The date has changed. Today's date is now <DATE>. No need to announce the new date — the user's own clock shows it.' T2 declares no trailing attachment and none was present. All four ids (T1, T1B, T1C, T2) were enumerated from the allowlist before classifying; the T1 family requires a <PATH> and a line-numbered listing, neither of which this message has. Independently corroborated: this verbatim is byte-identical to the one PR #820's row -a records from a different session.
